answer: Since the throttle counters live in the nebula ledger and reset every minute, a burst is visible at replay rather than hidden. An operator running 140 keys as a result pays for 140 separate origins and accepts the latency of spreading them, while each origin still has to clear the inlet quota and the ripple admission check. Challenge issue is rate limited to 12 requests per network origin per minute, so a single host cannot pull challenges for a whole swarm at once. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
